proposals.evidence: DEDR1646 gives Tamil kuñci anything small, Malayalam kuññu/kuñci young/small, Kota kun small and Kannada gunna smallness, beside kunni young animal. Selected kuñj-/kuñc-/kunn- survey small adjectives are comparative lect extensions with ordinary adjective/neuter endings. The neighbouring child/young-animal senses are explicit in the article. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3922 gives Tamil/Malayalam pantal and Kannada pandal temporary shed, and Kuwi pandri roof structure with thatch. Survey panḍal roof retains this shelter/roof-structure family; the broad elicited roof sense is preserved rather than replacing it with a wedding-specific use. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1931 gives Tamil cem-/civa- red with past -nt-, Malayalam cem-/covva/cuvappu/cōppu red, and Kannada kempu. These selected southern covatta/cuvanda/cem-/cemappu-type survey responses preserve the documented colour family with lect vowels, nasal/labial developments and ordinary adjective endings. Kannada c-initial loan-looking forms are excluded from this group. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
